full_judgment: 23. In the case of Erfan Ali vs Joynal Abedin Mia 35 DLR (AD) 216 it has been held that rent receipts are evidence of possession and may be used as collateral evidence of title. Section 110 of the Evidence Act provides a presumption of ownership in favour of person who is in possession of the property and possession follows title. Moreover, as per section 144A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, every entry in a record of rights prepared or revised under section 144 shall be evidence of the matter referred to in such entry and shall be presumed to be correct until it is proved by evidence to be incorrect. By producing SA Khatian No. 363 (Exhibit-Ga) defendant Nos. 1-2 contended that the SA Khatian was rightly prepared and finally published in the name of Amena Khatun on the basis of pattan dated 21-2-1947 (Exhibit-Ka). Though the plaintiff claimed that said deed of pattan was a product of forgery and the SA record was wrongly prepared and finally published in the name of Amena Khatun but she could not rebut the presumption of correctness of the SA Khatian by adducing any reliable evidence. Accordingly, it is to be presumed that deed of pattan dated 21-2-1947 has been acted upon and SA Khatian No. 363 was rightly prepared and finally published in the name of Amena Khatun. Though the plaintiff claimed that the title deeds by which defendant Nos. 1 and 2 claimed title to the suit land were forged documents but the original sale deeds were produced by the defendants and those were marked as exhibits without any objection from the plaintiff. Accordingly, it is to be presumed that those sale deeds are genuine documents. The defendants by producing oral and documentary evidence have been able to prove that they have been owning and possessing 0.4525 acre land for more than 12 years through their predecessors before filing of the suit and, as such, they have acquired title to and possession of 0.4525 acre land by way of adverse possession.
